decisions.reason: The original coassociativity calculation reversed tensor factors and omitted tensor signs. The repaired proof retains left coactions, evaluates the associated left action at the inverse, and uses a_ij=S(b_ij). The antipode reverses coproduct order and is involutive, so these coefficients obey the GL matrix identity and still generate A. The counit typo is also corrected. Statement and dependencies are unchanged; Milne Remark 4.1 and Theorem 4.9 were read to check conventions.

On Spec(F_p), an injective module need not be an injective abelian group. The general comparison instead uses module injectives being flasque, their acyclicity on every open, and the acyclic-resolution theorem. The repaired proof establishes f_*-acyclicity of flasque abelian sheaves and applies the module Grothendieck spectral sequence; AC supplies DC. The statement remains unchanged: its C-scheme shortcut is true, while the new proof covers arbitrary schemes.

F10 suppliers explicitly assume full AC, whereas F8/F9 use countable choice. The item already assumes full AC, so the hypotheses license the two-cell and dimension arguments; the defect is the inaccurate attribution of the choice strength. Corrected F11 and 8.1 to name full AC for constructibility, fibre dimension and the root suppliers. The SL2 chart transition remains t=1/z and the statements are unchanged.

The cited BCH theorem only gives an identity in a local neighborhood, not the global finite-product assertion in F3. Removed that dependency and derived the needed weight-component property by expanding each root exponential separately: all nonconstant terms strictly raise weights and the constant term is identity. Finite weight support makes each expansion finite. Stabilizer and closed-orbit conclusions and the statement are unchanged.

F3 as written attributes the natural Cech model and multiplication maps to a supplier whose Statement only lists cohomology modules. Added direct citations to the existing monomial-complex, graded sheaf, affine-vanishing and acyclic-cover suppliers and a local derivation: on U_I sections are localized degree-m polynomials, boundaries kill monomials with a nonnegative exponent, and multiplication localizes termwise. This licenses the coefficient pairing without a new claim or prerequisite item.

Both orbit and chart suppliers fix a simple root, so their invocation leaves rank zero uncovered. Added a separate proof: an empty root system makes the semisimple Lie algebra abelian and hence zero; connected smooth G is then a point, B=G, and the zeroth exterior-power Plucker line gives P^0. The quotient and product chart are identities. The original statement, including rank zero, is preserved.

The associated bundle of chi=-lambda is L_lambda, so the occurrence of -chi in step 2.2 is a sign error. Corrected it and explicitly checked the other essential-surjectivity direction: every character chi yields L_{-chi|T}, whose base fibre is C_chi. The evaluation isomorphism and full-faithfulness argument are unchanged, and the statement already has the correct sign.

F10 cites a lemma whose Statement exports flasqueness, not exact module extension by zero. Replaced that attribution by the actual abelian j_! interface and proved the module construction in step 3.0: restricted functions act on supported sections; stalks give exactness; the abelian adjunction preserves module-linearity stalkwise. The right adjoint restriction therefore preserves injectives and licenses both row exactness and localization of sheaf Ext. Koszul and conormal statements are unchanged.

The n=0 boundary is already correctly described in step 9.1, but F6 and the earlier general argument falsely apply negative-twist vanishing on P^0. Restricted the vanishing clauses to n>=1 and moved a complete evaluation-pairing proof for n=0 ahead of the dimension-shifting argument. Thus every use of negative H^0 vanishing now has n>=1, with the original all-n statement preserved.

The rank-one projection has target Spec(C), so it cannot be an identity on P^1. Corrected F6 and 2.1 to the unique map to a point, whose sole fibre is all of X_B. The example already states this correct fibre/base description, and its independent matrix calculation gives the same two charts and transition e_infinity=t^m e_0. Its line-bundle and canonical-bundle conclusions are unchanged.

The exact signs are present in thm-ext-is-hom-in-the-derived-category Proof 2.1 and Koszul sheaf-Ext Proof 1.2, but not in their exported Statements. Replaced F11 by its actual interface and supplied both calculations locally in 7.0: sigma_(p+1)=(-1)^(p+1)sigma_p for classical/derived Hom, the mixed-complex factor sigma_p(-1)^(pq), and s_(p+1)(-1)^p=s_p for Hodge duality. Thus the existing normalized orientation is justified without changing it. This is a citation/derivation presentation defect, not a false sign.

The rejection computes the sign of unscaled chain-map representatives, not the classical Koszul cochains used here. For c=n=1, the lift of the unscaled t map sends e_f wedge e_t to -e_f. But each degree-one classical cochain corresponds to minus that derived map (sigma_1=-1), and the degree-two classical cochain corresponds to minus the ambient derived map (sigma_2=-1). Hence their product is PLUS the raw classical ambient class. Generally its coefficient is sigma_c sigma_n (-1)^(cn)/sigma_(c+n)=1. With the Hodge/purity factor s_c sigma_c=(-1)^c and intrinsic (-1)^n, the result is (-1)^N times the ambient raw cochain, whose ordered Cech trace is (-1)^N. The final trace is 1. The generator-change determinants cancel against differential forms, and all formulas commute with scalar extension. The item is unchanged.
